facts.text: Vestaburg is an unincorporated community in Washington County, Pennsylvania, located along PA Route 88 and the Monongahela River.
The town grew around the Vesta Coal Company, a Jones & Laughlin subsidiary, with the Vesta No. 5 mine opening in 1908 and producing coal at a world‑record rate by 1918.
A post office opened in Vestaburg in 1916, marking the community’s rise alongside the booming bituminous coal industry.
Vestaburg sits on a compact 0.191 square‑mile area, bordered by the Monongahela River to the east and Fayette County across the waterway.
The landscape features undulating hills and floodplain along the Monongahela, giving the area a rugged yet scenic character typical of southwestern Pennsylvania.
Climate in Vestaburg follows a humid continental zone, with cold winters averaging 22°F lows and warm summers reaching 82°F highs.
